chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 331: The Black Tai Sui & Bai Lingmiao's Horrifying Pact
chapter_meta_description: A new bargain is struck. As Li Huowang celebrates the Mid-Autumn Festival, Bai Lingmiao learns the true weight of her contract with the Bei School Immortals.
og_title: The Moon Festival's Dark Side in Dao Gui Yi Xian
og_description: Isolated in a haunted temple, Bai Lingmiao learns the true cost of being a spirit-dancer while Li Huowang drunkenly toasts the moon.
twitter_title: The Immortals' Grip Tightens in Ch 331
twitter_description: Bai Lingmiao's servitude is made clear as Li Huowang celebrates the Mid-Autumn Festival with his hallucinations.

lore_anchors.definition: A grotesque, parasitic life-form. In this chapter, it gains the ability to emerge from its host on its own, a sign that it is growing stronger and more independent.
A major spirit entity that resides within Bai Lingmiao. It has three mouths under its red veil and displays moments of surprising humanity, such as recalling a 'father.'
A faction of spirit-immortals. Their powers are tied to the emotions they absorb, and they demand strict servitude from their human mediums.
A folk medium who serves as a vessel for spirits. The practice is shown here to be a form of slavery, with the medium forced to complete monthly tasks or face unknown consequences.
A major Chinese holiday celebrating the harvest and family reunion, centered around the full moon. Traditions include eating mooncakes and building earthen kilns.
A classic Chinese literacy primer composed of exactly 1,000 unique characters. Li Huowang uses it as a textbook, reciting the text as a form of training or control.
The imperial bureau that monitors and controls supernatural activity. Its officials take holidays, revealing a surprisingly mundane bureaucracy underneath its terrifying power.
